issues_in_prior_attempt: Screens are AI-generated and render as gibberish (monitors, the 'libertystone ONE' card, the dashboard). AI cannot draw real UI.
The hero balance '$59.00' is meaningless and the dashboard does not show the actual product.
The whole selling point (shares, ETFs and crypto in ONE place) never lands: no clear product, no words, no text.
With no VO and no on-screen text, a viewer cannot tell what LibertyStone is or that crypto sits beside shares and ETFs.
fixes: Frustration shots keep every screen blurred, angled or partial so nothing reads as gibberish; the overload comes from quantity and her reaction, not legible screens.

The solution shot uses a REAL designed dashboard mockup (built in HTML, captured, composited onto the laptop screen), not a generation. It shows one balance and a single holdings list that mixes Shares, ETFs and Crypto, so the USP is visible.
Replace '$59.00' with a realistic portfolio balance and a short holdings breakdown.
Lock the woman's face with a character reference image so she holds across clips.
End on the supplied LibertyStone logo animation plus one short line that states the USP, and a small risk line.
Recommend at least an on-screen tagline (and optionally one calm VO line); pure silence will not convey the crypto-alongside-shares message.

lessons: AI renders laptop UI as gibberish, so the dashboard is a real HTML render corner-pinned onto the screen quad with a CSS matrix3d homography (dashboard/composite-onscreen.mjs), composited onto the STILL plate first, then the whole still is animated with image2video: the screen stays glued and legible through the push-in with no wobble.
Key the navy out of the supplied wordmark with ffmpeg lumakey (threshold ~0.16) to drop it onto any ground with no seam; the raw PNG carries its own radial gradient that will not match a flat panel.
element2video with the character still as a visual reference holds her face across new scenes (overload, exhale); image2video is for the exact-match push-ins (opener, solution).
This ffmpeg build (imageio-ffmpeg static) has NO drawtext filter despite libfreetype in buildconf; render any on-screen text in the browser (playwright) to a transparent PNG and overlay it.

ElevenLabs MCP async calls (creative_generate_speech, creative_get_flow_run_status) failed this session with a protocol envelope error (missing resultType); simple calls (list_voices, create_flow) worked. Blocks TTS until resolved.
Seedance 2.5 Draft cost scales with duration (5s about 300, 6s 360, 26s with audio 1565, 30s with audio 1810). Quote from openart_model_cost, not a flat figure.

Never let the video model animate a composited screen: in the push-in it re-drew the dashboard and garbled the text ('LibertyStore', 'Eltsin'). Animate the plate with the screen kept black, then track the lid and warp the real UI on in post.

Track a laptop lid by measuring its edges, not by point tracking: LK points on the base drifted ~50 px by the end (base and tilted lid move differently under a dolly) and ECC on the bezel lost lock when her arm moved. Per-frame edge lines on all four sides, intersected, held 0.1 to 0.2 px.
The model's frame 0 is close to the start image but not pixel-identical; measure the screen on the video frames, not on the plate.
With the ElevenLabs connector unusable, the cloned-voice Seedance carrier (audio visualReference of a 12s sample) gave a word-perfect take in the same Australian voice.

A cloned Seedance VO is peaky (15.8 dB loudness-to-peak from plosives). A compressor did not help (its attack lets the transients through and it pulls the read down); a fast oversampled limiter driven +4 dB brought it to 11.4 and let the master reach -14 LUFS under the true-peak ceiling.

A prompted 'long, audible sigh' from Seedance comes back real but quiet: ~10 dB over a hissy floor. Denoise (afftdn), gate the room tone between the in-breath and the sigh, lift +6 dB, and duck the bed ~18 dB around it; cutting the clicks dead on the cut sells the release.
Whisper is unreliable at spelling letters read aloud (SMSF came back as 'SMSSF' from one model, 'SMSF' from another). Count the syllable bursts in the waveform instead.
Dashboard labels under ~40px at 2560 wide vanish at 480p-upscaled; size the words that carry the message for the shot, not for the mockup.

To fix how one word is said, re-take only that line on a short carrier with the same voice reference and spell the delivery out ('S M', short pause, 'S F'); take 2 and pick the one whose pitch and brightness match the ORIGINAL reading of the same sentence, not the neighbouring line (the narrator lifts on a payoff line). Verify the delivery from the waveform (check_smsf.py), not a transcript.

When a generated performance has one bad beat (an open-mouth breath that reads as a second sigh), map the expression across the clip and build the shot from the clean part: start on it, hold the last frame, and carry one eased push across both, computing the digital zoom per frame against the clip's own push so the move does not kink when the live part ends.
